newsitem.title: KUWAIT: United Arab Shipping joins service pool agreement.
newsitem.headline: United Arab Shipping joins service pool agreement.

text.p: The United Arab Shipping Co (UASC) has joined an agreement with Germany's DSR-Senator Lines GmbH and South Korea's Cho Yang Shipping Co Ltd to pool services, UASC said in a statement on Monday.
UASC "has entered a consortium agreement with the TRICON group, consisting of DSR-Senator Lines and Cho Yang, effective January 1997," the Kuwait-based firm said.
"The TRICON group in turn also has a cooperation with (South Korea's) Hanjin Shipping Co Ltd which will become a majority shareholder in DSR-Senator," it said.
Hanjin said last week it had agreed in principle to invest 75 million marks in DSR-Senator.
UASC said its agreement with TRICON was expected to pool 80 container ships with a combined capacity of almost 250,000 TEUs.

"During the initial phase of the agreement the service scope would include the America-Mediterranean-Asia service (AMA); the Asia-Middle East-Europe service (AEC) and the India-Pakistan- Express service (IPEX)," said UASC.

"The arrangements would allow UASC to offer in addition to its existing weekly service from Europe, Red Sea, Arabian Gulf, Far East and vice versa a direct weekly service between Asia and the U.S. East Coast, the Mediterranean and the U.S. East Coast, the Red Sea, the Arabian Gulf, Indian Subcontinent and vice versa," it added.
It said the new arrangements also expand UASC's geographical coverage of ports and adds direct coverage of China through the Shanghai call on the AMA service.
UASC will take delivery of 10 3,800-TEU container ships built by a Japanese consortium between March and November 1998.
UASC was formed in 1976 by the governments of Kuwait, Iraq, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Bahrain.
